title: Edge observability resilience and offline onboarding playbook
author: Marcos Delgado
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood’s recommended onboarding, verification, and escalation procedures for customers deploying edge or offline-capable telemetry collection with Redwood Private or Dedicated deployments. It focuses on ensuring telemetry continuity (metrics, traces, and request-level logs) when the customer’s network path to Redwood telemetry endpoints is interrupted, degraded, or intentionally air-gapped.

Audience:
- Customer Success Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Platform/Infra SRE, Customer Integrations teams.

Goals:
- Define telemetry delivery SLOs and verification tests for offline-capable collectors.
- Provide configuration templates for local buffering, encrypted disk persistence, and batched delivery.
- Standardize rollout verification and failure-mode drills.
- Provide an escalation matrix and runbook actions for delivery degradation and data-loss risk.

1) Non-goals:
- Replacing customer-specific compliance architectures; this playbook complements them.
- Prescribing exact collector projects (customers may use Fluentd, Vector, custom sidecars, or our Gateway agent).

2) Key definitions and SLOs:
- Telemetry Continuity SLO (customer-facing): 99.9% of telemetry events generated are successfully ingested within 72 hours.
- Real-time Telemetry SLO (platform-facing): 99.5% of events delivered within 30s under normal network conditions.
- Persistence Safety Threshold: local buffer must retain 48 hours of peak-event traffic with headroom >= 1.5x.
- Retry Backoff Policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max retry window 72 hours.

3) Roles and ownership:
- Customer Success (owner): onboarding coordination, acceptance criteria signoff, QBR reporting template.
- Integration/SE (owner): configuration guidance, test plan execution, verification artifacts.
- Customer Platform Team (owner): deploy collector agents, manage local storage and network policies.
- Eng-SRE (support): platform-side troubleshooting, ingestion backlog reconciliation, SLA adjustments.

4) Required customer-side capabilities (minimum):
- Persistent storage accessible to the collector agent with encryption-at-rest enabled.
- Outbound egress port allowances to Redwood telemetry endpoints OR a scheduled batch upload path (SFTP/HTTPS) approved in advance.
- A low-privilege service identity for the collector with scoped credentials and key rotation process.
- Synthetic traffic generator (simple script or load test) to produce deterministic test events.

5) Recommended configuration snippets (example YAML for Redwood Gateway agent):

# gateway-agent.yaml
collector:
  mode: offline-capable
  local_persistence:
    enabled: true
    path: /var/lib/redwood-gateway/buffer
    max_size_mb: 51200  # 50 GB (adjust per peak traffic)
    encryption: aes-gcm-256
  retention_hours: 72
delivery:
  endpoint: https://telemetry.redwood.example/v1/ingest
  batch_size: 1024
  max_concurrent_uploads: 4
  retry_policy:
    initial_backoff_s: 5
    max_backoff_s: 3600
    max_retry_window_hours: 72

Note: translate keys to the customer’s collector (Fluentd/Vector) equivalently.

6) Onboarding checklist (stages and acceptance criteria):
- Stage A: Pre-provisioning (customer completes)
  - Confirm storage path + encryption, agree on max retention sizing (artifact: sizing worksheet).
  - Confirm outbound egress or approved batch upload route.
  - Provide service identity/credentials to Redwood SE for test uploads.

- Stage B: Agent deployment (customer + SE)
  - Deploy agent in canary namespace/host (1–5% traffic).
  - Verify agent writes to local buffer; check permissions and disk usage.
  - Execute synthetic test for 1,000 events/min for 10 minutes.
  - Acceptance: agent persists events locally and marks events as queued.

- Stage C: Connectivity and delivery verification (customer + CS + Eng-SRE)
  - Run a simulated network partition (ingress blocked to Redwood endpoints) for 30 minutes.
  - Verify local buffer grows and no events are dropped.
  - Restore connectivity, verify backfill uploads complete and ingestion shows no duplicates or gaps.
  - Acceptance: Telemetry Continuity SLO met (all synthetic events ingested within 72 hours).

- Stage D: Scale and failure-mode tests (optional but recommended)
  - Simulate burst 5x peak for 1 hour; verify buffer headroom and upload behavior.
  - Test disk full condition: validate safe fail (agent rejects new events with clear logs) and recovery procedure.

7) Validation queries and dashboards (examples):
- Ingestion latency histogram (group by host/agent).
- Buffer utilization gauge per agent / host.
- Failed upload rate (5m rolling) > Alert at >= 0.5%.
- Backlog size in events and estimated hours to catch up.

Alert thresholds (recommended):
- P1: Backlog retention exceeds 80% of configured local persistence capacity OR estimated catch-up time > 48 hours.
- P2: Failed upload rate > 1% sustained for 15 minutes.
- P3: Agent process restarts > 3 times in 10 minutes.

8) Troubleshooting playbook (first 30 minutes):
1. Triage: Confirm whether issue is local (agent/host) or network (outbound to Redwood). Use agent status endpoint: curl http://localhost:9000/status
2. If network: capture tcpdump for outbound egress, check corporate proxy logs, verify DNS resolution to telemetry endpoint.
3. If local storage: df -h /var/lib/redwood-gateway; check agent logs for write errors and permissions.
4. Restart sequence: systemctl restart redwood-gateway-agent -> wait 30s -> check status. If restarts continue, escalate.

9) Escalation matrix (who to call and when):
- Level 1 (SE/CS handle) within 30 minutes: Collector misconfigurations, local disk warnings, authentication failures.
- Level 2 (Eng-SRE on call) within 2 hours: Large sustained backlogs, ingestion API 5xx responses, platform-side throttling.
- Level 3 (Platform Infra + Product) within 6 hours: Cross-region outage, storage corruption, data-loss risk.

Contact information (example):
- Customer Success: cs-team@redwood.ai (response target 60 minutes)
- Oncall Eng-SRE: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (pager for P1)
- Platform Incident Slack: #platform-telemetry-incidents

10) Backfill and deduplication guidance:
- Backfill window: Redwood ingestion accepts up to 72 hours of delayed events with automatic idempotence when events include stable event_id and timestamp.
- Deduplication keys: event_id + source_host + timestamp. When using custom collectors, ensure event_id is stable across retries.

11) Customer acceptance and handoff to support:
- Deliverables before handoff: signed acceptance checklist, synthetic test logs, buffer sizing worksheet, and runbook with local contact.
- Handoff meeting agenda: final test replay, alert subscriptions, escalation points, QBR cadence.

12) QBR metrics to track post-onboarding:
- Weekly Telemetry Continuity compliance (% events ingested within 72h).
- Mean backfill time for any partition incident.
- Number of agent-side incidents and mean time to resolution (MTTR).

13) Appendix: Example incident scenarios and recommended actions:
- Scenario A: Proxy misconfiguration blocks HTTPS egress
  - Action: Temporarily switch agent to scheduled batch upload over SFTP to the prearranged S3 endpoint; mark incident and coordinate with customer network to restore egress.

- Scenario B: Disk corruption detected on host
  - Action: Fail agent to standby host (if HA enabled), copy partial buffer to quarantine storage, engage Eng-SRE for partial ingestion reconciliation.

- Scenario C: Platform ingestion throttling observed (5xx from telemetry API)
  - Action: Throttle client-side concurrent uploads to 1, open ticket with Eng-SRE, and enable priority routing for critical customer events (per contract).

Artifacts and templates (links to attach in Confluence):
- Buffer sizing worksheet (CSV template)
- Synthetic event generator (Python script)
- Acceptance checklist (PDF)

Notes and change history:
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft created by Marcos Delgado.
- 2026-03-04: Added retry policy and backlog alert thresholds per Eng-SRE feedback.
- 2026-07-14: Expanded verification tests and clarified deduplication guidance after two customer onboards.

End of document.
